description: Assess toxicological risk from hazard identification through dose-response analysis, exposure characterization, and risk quantification.

steps.description: Identify the chemical or agent hazard by reviewing toxicological databases, animal study summaries, and epidemiological evidence.

inputs.name: agent-name
inputs.desc: Name or CAS number of the substance under review

inputs.name: exposure-context
inputs.desc: Where and how exposure occurs (occupational, environmental, dietary)

outputs.name: hazard-profile
outputs.desc: Summary of known toxic endpoints, target organs, and mechanisms

outputs.name: evidence-table
outputs.desc: Table of studies with species, route, dose, and observed effects

process: Search toxicological databases (IRIS, ATSDR, ECHA) for the substance
Compile animal and human study results by endpoint and route of exposure
Classify each endpoint by strength of evidence (sufficient, limited, inadequate)
Produce the hazard profile with the evidence table

steps.description: Compile dose-response data from multiple studies and determine the critical study and critical effect.

inputs.name: evidence-table
inputs.desc: Table of studies with species, route, dose, and effects

inputs.name: hazard-profile
inputs.desc: Hazard profile identifying the endpoints of concern

outputs.name: dose-response-dataset
outputs.desc: Structured dose-response data from the critical study

outputs.name: critical-effect-summary
outputs.desc: The selected critical effect, its NOAEL or LOAEL, and justification

process: Rank studies by relevance (species, route, duration, quality)
Select the critical study and critical effect based on the most sensitive endpoint
Extract dose-response pairs from the critical study
Identify the NOAEL, LOAEL, or benchmark dose from the data

steps.description: Derive the reference dose (RfD) or benchmark dose (BMD) from the dose-response data using appropriate uncertainty factors.

inputs.name: dose-response-dataset
inputs.desc: Dose-response data from the critical study

inputs.name: critical-effect-summary
inputs.desc: The critical effect and its point of departure

outputs.name: reference-dose
outputs.desc: The derived RfD or BMD with units and basis

outputs.name: uncertainty-factor-table
outputs.desc: Table of applied uncertainty factors with justification for each

process: Select the point of departure (NOAEL, LOAEL, or BMDL)
Apply uncertainty factors for interspecies, intraspecies, duration, LOAEL-to-NOAEL, and data gaps
Calculate the reference dose by dividing the point of departure by the composite uncertainty factor
Document the rationale for each factor

steps.description: Characterize the exposure pathways and estimate the magnitude, frequency, and duration of exposure for the population of concern.

inputs.name: agent-name
inputs.desc: Name or CAS number of the substance

outputs.name: exposure-estimate
outputs.desc: Quantified exposure by pathway (mg/kg/day or equivalent)

outputs.name: exposure-scenario
outputs.desc: Description of the exposure scenario including population, duration, and route

process: Map the exposure pathways from source to receptor (ingestion, inhalation, dermal)
Estimate concentrations in each medium (air, water, soil, food)
Apply intake parameters (body weight, inhalation rate, contact rate) for the target population
Calculate the average daily dose for each pathway and the total

steps.description: Compute the hazard quotient or margin of exposure by comparing the exposure estimate to the reference dose.

inputs.name: reference-dose
inputs.desc: The derived reference dose or benchmark dose

outputs.name: risk-characterization
outputs.desc: Hazard quotient, margin of exposure, and risk classification

outputs.name: risk-drivers
outputs.desc: Identification of the pathways and populations driving the risk

process: Divide the exposure estimate by the reference dose to compute the hazard quotient
Classify risk as acceptable (HQ < 1) or of concern (HQ >= 1)
Identify which pathways and populations contribute most to the total risk
Compute the margin of exposure for cancer endpoints where applicable

steps.description: Assess the uncertainties in the risk assessment including data gaps, model assumptions, and variability in the exposed population.

inputs.name: uncertainty-factor-table
inputs.desc: Applied uncertainty factors and their justification

outputs.name: uncertainty-narrative
outputs.desc: Qualitative and quantitative description of key uncertainties

outputs.name: confidence-rating
outputs.desc: Overall confidence in the risk estimate (high, medium, low) with justification

process: Catalog the data gaps in hazard identification, dose-response, and exposure
Evaluate how each uncertainty affects the direction and magnitude of the risk estimate
Perform sensitivity analysis on the most influential parameters
Assign an overall confidence rating

steps.description: Compile the full risk assessment into a structured report following regulatory formatting conventions.

outputs.name: risk-assessment-report
outputs.desc: The complete risk assessment document

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page summary of hazard, exposure, risk, and confidence

process: Structure the report: executive summary, hazard identification, dose-response, exposure, risk characterization, uncertainty
Write each section referencing the supporting data
Include the executive summary with the bottom-line risk conclusion
Format tables and figures for the regulatory audience

description: Analyze a metagenomic dataset from raw reads through taxonomy, diversity, and functional profiling.

steps.description: Quality-filter metagenomic reads by trimming adapters, removing low-quality bases, and filtering host contamination.

inputs.name: raw-reads
inputs.desc: FASTQ files from the sequencing run

inputs.name: host-reference
inputs.desc: Host genome for contamination removal (if applicable)

outputs.name: filtered-reads
outputs.desc: Quality-filtered FASTQ files ready for analysis

outputs.name: qc-report
outputs.desc: Summary of read counts, quality scores, and filtering statistics

process: Run adapter trimming and quality filtering (Trimmomatic, fastp, or equivalent)
Remove host-derived reads by mapping against the host reference genome
Generate quality metrics before and after filtering
Produce the QC report with pass/fail thresholds

steps.description: Assign taxonomy to filtered reads using 16S marker gene or whole-genome shotgun methods.

inputs.name: taxonomy-database
inputs.desc: Reference database for classification (Silva, GTDB, Kraken2 DB)

outputs.name: taxonomy-table
outputs.desc: OTU or ASV table with taxonomic assignments and counts per sample

outputs.name: classification-summary
outputs.desc: Fraction classified, dominant taxa, and unclassified rate

process: Select the classification approach (amplicon: DADA2/QIIME2; shotgun: Kraken2/MetaPhlAn)
Run the classifier against the reference database
Build the taxonomy count table at each rank (phylum through species)
Summarize classification rates and dominant taxa

steps.description: Compute alpha and beta diversity metrics from the taxonomy table.

inputs.name: taxonomy-table
inputs.desc: OTU or ASV table with counts per sample

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Metadata for each sample (group, site, timepoint)

outputs.name: alpha-diversity
outputs.desc: Per-sample richness (observed, Chao1) and evenness (Shannon, Simpson)

outputs.name: beta-diversity-matrix
outputs.desc: Pairwise distance matrix (Bray-Curtis, UniFrac) with ordination coordinates

process: Rarefy or normalize the count table to even depth
Compute alpha diversity indices for each sample
Compute beta diversity distances between all sample pairs
Run ordination (PCoA or NMDS) and test group separation (PERMANOVA)

steps.description: Identify taxa that differ significantly between experimental groups.

outputs.name: differential-taxa-list
outputs.desc: List of significantly enriched or depleted taxa with effect sizes and adjusted p-values

outputs.name: abundance-plots
outputs.desc: Visualization of differential taxa across groups

process: Select the statistical method (DESeq2, ALDEx2, ANCOM, LEfSe)
Run the differential abundance test with appropriate corrections for compositionality
Apply multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg)
Produce ranked lists and plots of significant taxa

steps.description: Predict the functional potential of the microbial community from taxonomy or assembled genes.

outputs.name: pathway-abundance-table
outputs.desc: Predicted metabolic pathway abundances per sample

outputs.name: functional-summary
outputs.desc: Key functional categories and their differential presence across groups

process: For marker gene data, run PICRUSt2 or Tax4Fun to infer gene content from taxonomy
For shotgun data, run HUMAnN3 to quantify pathway abundances directly from reads
Map gene families to metabolic pathways (MetaCyc, KEGG)
Summarize the functional profile and identify differentially abundant pathways

steps.description: Compile the metagenomics analysis into a structured report with taxonomy, diversity, differential abundance, and functional results.

outputs.name: metagenomics-report
outputs.desc: The complete analysis report with methods, results, and figures

outputs.name: supplementary-tables
outputs.desc: Full taxonomy, diversity, and pathway tables for archival

process: Structure the report: methods, QC summary, taxonomy, diversity, differential abundance, function
Embed key figures (bar plots, ordination, heatmaps, forest plots)
Write interpretive text for each section
Package supplementary tables for data archival

description: Process photometric observations from raw images through calibration, source detection, photometry, and light curve fitting.

steps.description: Calibrate raw CCD images by subtracting bias, dark current, and dividing by the flat field.

inputs.name: raw-science-frames
inputs.desc: Raw FITS images from the observing run

inputs.name: calibration-frames
inputs.desc: Bias, dark, and flat-field frames taken during the run

outputs.name: calibrated-frames
outputs.desc: Science frames with instrumental signatures removed

outputs.name: calibration-log
outputs.desc: Record of which calibration frames were applied and quality metrics

process: Build master bias from the median of bias frames and subtract from all other frames
Build master dark (bias-subtracted, exposure-scaled) and subtract from science and flat frames
Build master flat from normalized flat frames and divide each science frame by it
Log each step and flag frames with anomalous statistics

steps.description: Detect point sources in calibrated images and produce an initial source catalog with positions and instrumental fluxes.

outputs.name: source-catalog
outputs.desc: Table of detected sources with pixel coordinates, instrumental magnitudes, and SNR

outputs.name: detection-mask
outputs.desc: Image mask showing detected sources and rejected artifacts

process: Estimate the sky background and its variation across each frame
Run source extraction (SExtractor, DAOFind, or equivalent) at the specified threshold
Reject cosmic rays, hot pixels, and extended artifacts
Produce the source catalog sorted by brightness

steps.description: Perform aperture photometry or PSF-fitting photometry on detected sources to measure precise instrumental magnitudes.

inputs.name: source-catalog
inputs.desc: Catalog of detected sources with positions

outputs.name: photometry-table
outputs.desc: Instrumental magnitudes with uncertainties for each source on each frame

outputs.name: photometry-diagnostics
outputs.desc: Growth curves, PSF model, and aperture correction values

process: Choose aperture photometry (isolated fields) or PSF fitting (crowded fields)
For aperture: measure flux in concentric apertures, determine optimal aperture, apply aperture correction
For PSF: build the PSF model from bright stars, fit to all sources, subtract neighbors
Record instrumental magnitudes and their uncertainties

steps.description: Calibrate instrumental magnitudes to a standard photometric system using standard star observations or catalog cross-matching.

inputs.name: standard-catalog
inputs.desc: Reference photometric catalog (Landolt, APASS, PS1, Gaia)

outputs.name: calibrated-magnitudes
outputs.desc: Magnitudes on the standard system with zero-point and color terms

outputs.name: calibration-residuals
outputs.desc: Residuals against the standard stars and the derived transformation

process: Cross-match detected sources with the standard catalog
Fit the zero point, extinction coefficient, and color term
Apply the transformation to all sources
Report the residuals and RMS of the calibration

steps.description: Build a time-series light curve for a target source from calibrated multi-epoch photometry.

inputs.name: target-coordinates
inputs.desc: Sky coordinates of the target source

outputs.name: light-curve
outputs.desc: Time-series of calibrated magnitudes with timestamps and uncertainties

outputs.name: variability-statistics
outputs.desc: Reduced chi-squared, amplitude, and period estimate if periodic

process: Extract the target magnitude from each epoch
Compute differential photometry against stable comparison stars to reduce systematics
Assemble the light curve with barycentric time correction
Compute variability statistics and search for periodicity (Lomb-Scargle)

steps.description: Fit a physical model to the light curve (transit, eclipsing binary, pulsation, or transient decay).

inputs.name: model-type
inputs.desc: The type of model to fit (transit, eclipse, sinusoidal, exponential)

outputs.name: best-fit-parameters
outputs.desc: Fitted model parameters with uncertainties

outputs.name: model-comparison
outputs.desc: Residuals, reduced chi-squared, and BIC for model comparison

process: Select the physical model appropriate to the variability type
Fit the model using least-squares or MCMC sampling
Compute parameter uncertainties from the posterior or covariance matrix
Compare the fit residuals to the photometric uncertainties

steps.description: Compile the photometric analysis into a report with calibration details, light curves, model fits, and interpretation.

inputs.name: best-fit-parameters
inputs.desc: Fitted model parameters and comparison metrics

outputs.name: photometry-report
outputs.desc: Complete photometry report with methods, results, and figures

outputs.name: data-products
outputs.desc: Machine-readable light curve and model parameters for archival

process: Structure the report: observations, reduction, calibration, light curve, model, interpretation
Embed key figures (finding chart, light curve, model overlay, residuals)
Write the physical interpretation of the model parameters
Package data products in standard formats (CSV, VOTable)

description: Validate a candidate biomarker from cohort assembly through ROC analysis, cutoff determination, and independent validation.

steps.description: Define the clinical question the biomarker is intended to answer, including the target condition, intended use, and clinical context.

inputs.name: candidate-biomarker
inputs.desc: The biomarker under evaluation (analyte, gene, imaging feature)

inputs.name: clinical-context
inputs.desc: The disease, population, and clinical decision the biomarker would inform

outputs.name: clinical-question
outputs.desc: Structured clinical question (screening, diagnosis, prognosis, or monitoring)

outputs.name: performance-targets
outputs.desc: Minimum acceptable sensitivity, specificity, and PPV for clinical utility

process: Classify the intended use as screening, diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment monitoring
Define the target condition and the reference standard for case ascertainment
Set the minimum performance targets based on clinical consequence of false positives and negatives
Document the clinical question in structured format

steps.description: Assemble the case-control cohort for biomarker evaluation, applying inclusion and exclusion criteria.

inputs.name: clinical-question
inputs.desc: The structured clinical question defining cases and controls

inputs.name: sample-source
inputs.desc: The biobank, registry, or clinical site providing specimens

outputs.name: study-cohort
outputs.desc: Enrolled cases and controls with demographics and clinical data

outputs.name: cohort-characteristics
outputs.desc: Table 1: baseline characteristics by group

process: Apply inclusion and exclusion criteria to identify eligible cases and controls
Match controls on relevant confounders (age, sex, comorbidities) if appropriate
Verify the reference standard diagnosis for each case
Compile demographics and clinical characteristics

steps.description: Construct the receiver operating characteristic curve and compute the area under the curve for the biomarker.

inputs.name: study-cohort
inputs.desc: Cases and controls with biomarker measurements

outputs.name: roc-curve-data
outputs.desc: Sensitivity and specificity at each threshold, AUC with 95% CI

outputs.name: auc-comparison
outputs.desc: AUC compared to existing biomarkers or clinical scores if available

process: Plot the ROC curve by sweeping the biomarker threshold
Compute the AUC with bootstrapped 95% confidence interval
Test if AUC differs significantly from chance (0.5) and from comparator biomarkers
Visualize the ROC curve with the operating point

steps.description: Determine the optimal cutoff for the biomarker using the Youden index or clinical utility criteria.

inputs.name: roc-curve-data
inputs.desc: Sensitivity and specificity at each threshold

outputs.name: optimal-cutoff
outputs.desc: The selected cutoff value with sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV

outputs.name: classification-table
outputs.desc: 2x2 contingency table at the chosen cutoff

process: Compute the Youden index (sensitivity + specificity - 1) at each threshold
Identify the threshold maximizing the Youden index
Check if this cutoff meets the minimum performance targets
Compute PPV and NPV at the chosen cutoff using the study prevalence

steps.description: Test the biomarker cutoff in an independent validation cohort to confirm performance.

inputs.name: optimal-cutoff
inputs.desc: The cutoff derived from the discovery cohort

inputs.name: validation-cohort-data
inputs.desc: Independent cohort with biomarker measurements and diagnoses

outputs.name: validation-performance
outputs.desc: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and AUC in the validation cohort

outputs.name: calibration-assessment
outputs.desc: Observed vs predicted risk across deciles (calibration plot)

process: Apply the discovery cutoff to the validation cohort without re-optimization
Compute classification performance metrics
Construct the calibration plot to assess agreement between predicted and observed risk
Compare validation AUC to discovery AUC and test for significant degradation

steps.description: Compile the biomarker validation study into a STARD-compliant report.

inputs.name: validation-performance
inputs.desc: Performance metrics from the validation cohort

inputs.name: roc-curve-data
inputs.desc: ROC analysis from the discovery cohort

outputs.name: biomarker-report
outputs.desc: Complete validation report following STARD guidelines

outputs.name: clinical-recommendation
outputs.desc: Recommendation on clinical adoption readiness

process: Structure the report following STARD (Standards for Reporting of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies)
Include the flow diagram of participant enrollment
Present discovery and validation results side by side
State the clinical recommendation with confidence level

description: Set up and analyze a computational fluid dynamics simulation from geometry definition through validation against experimental data.

steps.description: Define the computational domain geometry and generate the mesh with appropriate resolution for the flow features of interest.

inputs.name: geometry-definition
inputs.desc: CAD model or geometric description of the domain

inputs.name: flow-conditions
inputs.desc: Expected Reynolds number, Mach number, and key flow features

outputs.name: computational-mesh
outputs.desc: Volumetric mesh with boundary layer refinement and quality metrics

outputs.name: mesh-quality-report
outputs.desc: Cell count, skewness, aspect ratio, and y+ estimate

process: Import or construct the geometry and define the fluid domain boundaries
Set mesh sizing: global element size, boundary layer inflation, and feature-based refinement
Generate the mesh and check quality metrics (skewness < 0.9, aspect ratio < 100)
Estimate the wall y+ for the intended turbulence model and adjust if needed

steps.description: Select the turbulence model based on the flow regime, computational budget, and accuracy requirements.

inputs.name: flow-conditions
inputs.desc: Reynolds number, flow type (internal, external, free shear), and key phenomena

outputs.name: turbulence-model-config
outputs.desc: Selected model (k-epsilon, k-omega SST, SA, LES, DES) with parameters

outputs.name: model-justification
outputs.desc: Rationale for the selection citing the flow physics and mesh resolution

process: Classify the flow (attached, separated, transitional, reacting, compressible)
Match flow class to model capability (RANS for attached, LES for large separation, DES for mixed)
Verify the mesh resolution supports the selected model (y+ requirements, LES filter width)
Document the model choice and its known limitations for this flow

steps.description: Define the boundary conditions for the simulation including inlets, outlets, walls, and symmetry planes.

inputs.name: computational-mesh
inputs.desc: The meshed domain with named boundaries

inputs.name: flow-conditions
inputs.desc: Inlet velocity/pressure, temperature, and turbulence intensity

outputs.name: boundary-setup
outputs.desc: Complete set of boundary conditions for each named surface

outputs.name: initial-conditions
outputs.desc: Initial field values and solver settings for startup

process: Assign physical type to each boundary (velocity inlet, pressure outlet, no-slip wall, symmetry)
Set inlet profiles (uniform, parabolic, or mapped from experimental data)
Set turbulence inlet conditions (intensity and length scale or turbulent viscosity ratio)
Define initial conditions and solver parameters (time step, convergence criteria)

steps.description: Run the CFD solver to convergence, monitoring residuals and key physical quantities.

outputs.name: converged-solution
outputs.desc: The converged flow field (velocity, pressure, turbulence quantities)

outputs.name: convergence-history
outputs.desc: Residual histories and monitor point values over iterations

process: Initialize the flow field and begin iterating
Monitor residuals (continuity, momentum, turbulence) and physical monitors (drag, mass flow)
Adjust under-relaxation or time stepping if convergence stalls
Declare convergence when residuals drop below threshold and monitors stabilize

steps.description: Extract flow quantities of interest from the converged solution (velocity profiles, pressure distributions, forces, heat transfer).

inputs.name: extraction-plan
inputs.desc: List of quantities, locations, and surfaces to extract

outputs.name: extracted-quantities
outputs.desc: Tabulated flow data at the requested locations and surfaces

outputs.name: flow-visualizations
outputs.desc: Contour plots, streamlines, and vector fields

process: Extract line and surface data at the specified locations
Compute derived quantities (wall shear stress, heat flux, vorticity)
Integrate forces and moments on bodies of interest
Generate visualization images (contours, streamlines, isosurfaces)

steps.description: Compare simulation results against experimental data to assess accuracy and identify discrepancies.

inputs.name: experimental-data
inputs.desc: Measured values from wind tunnel, PIV, or other experiments

outputs.name: validation-metrics
outputs.desc: Quantitative comparison (RMS error, correlation, bias) at each measurement station

outputs.name: discrepancy-analysis
outputs.desc: Identification of regions where simulation and experiment disagree and likely causes

process: Interpolate simulation results to experimental measurement locations
Compute point-by-point and integrated comparison metrics
Identify regions of good and poor agreement
Attribute discrepancies to mesh resolution, turbulence model, boundary conditions, or experimental uncertainty

steps.description: Compile the CFD study into a report documenting the setup, results, validation, and conclusions.

outputs.name: simulation-report
outputs.desc: Complete CFD study report

outputs.name: lessons-learned
outputs.desc: Notes on what worked, what to change, and recommended next steps

process: Structure the report: problem definition, mesh, model, boundary conditions, convergence, results, validation
Embed the key figures and validation plots
State the confidence in the results given the validation metrics
Document lessons learned and recommendations for follow-on studies

description: Analyze an archaeological site from stratigraphic documentation through artifact cataloging, dating, spatial analysis, and site interpretation.

steps.description: Document the site stratigraphy by recording layer sequences, interfaces, and depositional contexts.

inputs.name: excavation-records
inputs.desc: Field notes, section drawings, and photographs from the excavation

inputs.name: site-grid
inputs.desc: Site grid coordinates and unit designations

outputs.name: harris-matrix
outputs.desc: Stratigraphic sequence diagram showing the temporal relationships between contexts

outputs.name: context-register
outputs.desc: Register of all contexts with descriptions, elevations, and soil characteristics

process: Assign context numbers to each distinct stratigraphic unit
Record the physical characteristics (color, texture, inclusions) of each context
Determine the stratigraphic relationships (above, below, cuts, fill) between contexts
Construct the Harris matrix from the observed relationships

steps.description: Catalog excavated artifacts by context, recording material, type, dimensions, and condition.

inputs.name: excavated-artifacts
inputs.desc: Artifacts recovered from each context with find numbers

outputs.name: artifact-catalog
outputs.desc: Database of artifacts with context, type, material, dimensions, and condition

outputs.name: type-frequency-table
outputs.desc: Counts of artifact types per context and phase

process: Wash, label, and photograph each artifact
Classify by material (ceramic, lithic, bone, metal, glass) and type
Record dimensions, weight, condition, and any diagnostic features
Compile the catalog and compute type frequencies by context

steps.description: Select and apply dating methods appropriate to the site and materials, combining absolute and relative techniques.

inputs.name: datable-materials
inputs.desc: Charcoal, bone, ceramic, or other datable samples from each context

outputs.name: chronology-table
outputs.desc: Absolute and relative dates for each phase or context

outputs.name: dating-method-notes
outputs.desc: Methods used, lab IDs, and calibration details for each date

process: Identify datable materials from each major context
Select appropriate methods (radiocarbon, thermoluminescence, typological seriation)
Submit samples and calibrate results (IntCal for radiocarbon)
Integrate absolute dates with the stratigraphic sequence to build the site chronology

steps.description: Analyze the spatial distribution of artifacts and features across the site to identify activity areas and site structure.

inputs.name: artifact-catalog
inputs.desc: Artifacts with 3D coordinates and context assignments

outputs.name: density-maps
outputs.desc: Kernel density maps of artifact types across the site

outputs.name: activity-area-interpretation
outputs.desc: Identified clusters and their functional interpretation

process: Plot artifact locations in the site grid by type and material
Compute density distributions and identify clusters (nearest neighbor, Ripley's K)
Relate clusters to features (hearths, pits, walls) for functional interpretation
Map activity areas (cooking, tool production, storage, refuse disposal)

steps.description: Reconstruct the processes that formed and transformed the archaeological deposits.

outputs.name: formation-narrative
outputs.desc: Narrative of how the site was formed, occupied, abandoned, and transformed

outputs.name: taphonomic-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of post-depositional disturbance and its effect on the record

process: Classify each context as primary deposition, secondary fill, or natural accumulation
Identify evidence of post-depositional processes (bioturbation, plowing, erosion, looting)
Assess the integrity of each phase based on artifact refitting, fragmentation, and weathering
Construct the formation narrative from earliest to latest event

steps.description: Compare the site with regional sequences and contemporaneous sites to place it in broader context.

outputs.name: regional-comparison
outputs.desc: How the site fits within the regional cultural sequence

outputs.name: significance-assessment
outputs.desc: The site's contribution to understanding regional history

process: Compare the artifact assemblage with published regional type series
Place each phase within the regional chronological framework
Identify parallels and divergences with contemporaneous sites
Assess the site's significance for regional questions

steps.description: Compile the site analysis into a publication-quality report following disciplinary standards.

outputs.name: site-report
outputs.desc: Complete archaeological site report with stratigraphy, finds, dating, and interpretation

outputs.name: archive-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of the physical and digital archive for deposition

process: Structure the report: introduction, methods, stratigraphy, finds, dating, spatial analysis, interpretation
Include the Harris matrix, plans, sections, photographs, and artifact illustrations
Write the interpretive synthesis connecting evidence to questions
Compile the archive inventory for repository deposition

description: Profile the metabolome from sample extraction through spectral acquisition, metabolite identification, and multivariate analysis.

steps.description: Extract metabolites from biological samples using the appropriate solvent system and sample preparation method.

inputs.name: biological-samples
inputs.desc: Tissue, plasma, urine, or cell pellet samples with metadata

inputs.name: extraction-protocol
inputs.desc: Solvent system and method (methanol-chloroform, acetonitrile, solid phase)

outputs.name: metabolite-extracts
outputs.desc: Prepared extracts ready for instrumental analysis

outputs.name: extraction-qc
outputs.desc: Recovery rates, blank results, and preparation batch information

process: Aliquot samples and add internal standards
Apply the extraction protocol (solvent addition, vortex, centrifuge, evaporate)
Reconstitute in the appropriate solvent for the analytical platform
Prepare pooled QC samples and blanks

steps.description: Acquire NMR or mass spectrometry data from the metabolite extracts with appropriate quality controls.

inputs.name: instrument-method
inputs.desc: Acquisition parameters (NMR pulse sequence, LC-MS gradient, ionization mode)

outputs.name: raw-spectra
outputs.desc: Raw spectral data files from the instrument

outputs.name: acquisition-log
outputs.desc: Run order, QC injections, and instrument performance metrics

process: Set up the instrument method and verify with a system suitability standard
Run samples in randomized order with QC injections every 10 samples
Monitor retention time stability and signal intensity drift
Export raw data files and the acquisition log

steps.description: Process and align the raw spectral data across samples to produce a feature table.

inputs.name: raw-spectra
inputs.desc: Raw spectral data from all samples

inputs.name: processing-parameters
inputs.desc: Peak detection, alignment, and gap-filling parameters

outputs.name: feature-table
outputs.desc: Sample-by-feature matrix of peak areas or intensities

outputs.name: processing-report
outputs.desc: Number of features detected, alignment quality, and missing value rate

process: Detect peaks or bins across all samples (XCMS, MZmine, or NMR bucketing)
Align retention times or chemical shifts across the sample set
Fill gaps where a feature was detected in some samples but not others
Filter features by blank ratio, QC CV, and minimum detection frequency

steps.description: Identify metabolites by matching spectral features against reference databases and standards.

inputs.name: feature-table
inputs.desc: Detected features with m/z, retention time, and/or chemical shift

inputs.name: reference-databases
inputs.desc: HMDB, METLIN, MassBank, or in-house library

outputs.name: annotated-feature-table
outputs.desc: Features annotated with putative metabolite identifications and confidence levels

outputs.name: identification-evidence
outputs.desc: Matching scores, MS2 mirror plots, and confidence classification (MSI levels 1-4)

process: Match accurate mass and isotope pattern against databases (MSI level 3)
Compare MS2 fragmentation spectra against spectral libraries (MSI level 2)
Confirm with authentic standards where available (MSI level 1)
Annotate the feature table with the best identification and confidence level

steps.description: Run multivariate statistical analysis on the metabolomics data to identify group-level patterns and significant metabolites.

inputs.name: sample-metadata
inputs.desc: Group assignments and covariates for each sample

outputs.name: multivariate-results
outputs.desc: PCA scores, PLS-DA model, VIP scores, and permutation test results

outputs.name: significant-metabolites
outputs.desc: List of metabolites driving group separation with fold change and adjusted p-value

process: Normalize (total ion current, probabilistic quotient), log-transform, and scale (Pareto or auto)
Run unsupervised PCA to check for outliers and batch effects
Run supervised PLS-DA and validate with permutation testing and cross-validation
Extract VIP scores and run univariate tests (t-test, Wilcoxon) with FDR correction

steps.description: Compile the metabolomics study into a report with methods, quality metrics, identified metabolites, and biological interpretation.

outputs.name: metabolomics-report
outputs.desc: Complete metabolomics study report

outputs.name: pathway-context
outputs.desc: Mapping of significant metabolites to biological pathways (KEGG, Reactome)

process: Structure the report: sample prep, acquisition, processing, identification, statistics, biology
Embed key figures (PCA, PLS-DA, volcano plot, heatmap, pathway map)
Map significant metabolites to biological pathways for interpretation
State the conclusions with the strength and limitations of the evidence

description: Investigate a disease outbreak from case definition through source identification, hypothesis testing, and control recommendations.

steps.description: Establish the case definition specifying the clinical, temporal, and geographic criteria for inclusion.

inputs.name: initial-reports
inputs.desc: Early reports of illness including symptoms, timing, and location

inputs.name: clinical-presentation
inputs.desc: Description of the illness (symptoms, lab findings, severity)

outputs.name: case-definition
outputs.desc: Confirmed, probable, and suspect case criteria

outputs.name: case-classification-guide
outputs.desc: Decision tree for classifying each reported case

process: Review initial clinical presentations to identify the syndrome
Define confirmed cases (lab-confirmed), probable (clinical + epidemiologic link), and suspect (clinical only)
Set the time and place boundaries for the investigation
Document the classification guide for field use

steps.description: Compile the line list of all cases with demographic, clinical, exposure, and outcome information.

inputs.name: case-reports
inputs.desc: Individual case reports from surveillance, hospitals, and labs

outputs.name: line-list
outputs.desc: Structured table: one row per case with ID, demographics, onset, exposures, outcome

outputs.name: attack-rates
outputs.desc: Attack rates by group (age, sex, location, exposure)

process: Collect case reports from all reporting sources
Abstract each case into the line list format with standardized fields
Classify each case as confirmed, probable, or suspect
Calculate overall and group-specific attack rates

steps.description: Construct and interpret the epidemic curve to determine the pattern of spread and estimate the incubation period.

inputs.name: line-list
inputs.desc: Case line list with onset dates

outputs.name: epidemic-curve
outputs.desc: Histogram of case counts by onset date with outbreak pattern classification

outputs.name: incubation-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated incubation period range based on the curve shape and known exposures

process: Plot case counts by date of onset using appropriate time intervals
Classify the curve shape (point source, continuous, propagated, intermittent)
Estimate the probable exposure window by back-calculating from onset dates
Estimate the incubation period from cases with known single exposures

steps.description: Generate hypotheses about the source and mode of transmission based on descriptive epidemiology.

outputs.name: hypothesis-list
outputs.desc: Ranked list of plausible source and transmission hypotheses

outputs.name: exposure-comparison
outputs.desc: Exposure frequencies among cases vs non-cases (2x2 tables)

process: Interview cases about common exposures (food, water, events, contacts, travel)
Compare exposure frequencies between cases and non-cases
Identify exposures with the highest relative risk or odds ratio
Rank hypotheses by strength of the descriptive association

steps.description: Test the source hypothesis with an analytical study (case-control or cohort) and compute the measure of association.

outputs.name: study-results
outputs.desc: Odds ratios or relative risks with confidence intervals and p-values for each exposure

outputs.name: dose-response-check
outputs.desc: Dose-response relationship if exposure has graded levels

process: Select the study design (case-control for rare outcome, cohort for defined population)
Enroll controls (matched or unmatched) or define the cohort
Compute the odds ratio or relative risk with 95% confidence intervals
Test for dose-response and confounding by stratified or multivariable analysis

steps.description: Recommend control measures based on the identified source and mode of transmission.

outputs.name: control-recommendations
outputs.desc: Specific actions to stop transmission (recall, closure, prophylaxis, isolation)

outputs.name: monitoring-plan
outputs.desc: Plan to monitor the effect of interventions on case counts

process: Match the identified source to the appropriate intervention (remove source, interrupt transmission, protect susceptibles)
Prioritize actions by urgency and feasibility
Define success criteria (declining case counts, negative environmental samples)
Establish the monitoring and follow-up schedule

steps.description: Compile the outbreak investigation into a report documenting the investigation steps, findings, and outcomes.

inputs.name: epidemic-curve
inputs.desc: Epidemic curve with intervention timing annotated

outputs.name: investigation-report
outputs.desc: Complete outbreak investigation report

outputs.name: lessons-learned
outputs.desc: What worked, what to improve, and recommendations for prevention

process: Structure the report: background, methods, results (descriptive and analytical), discussion, recommendations
Include the epidemic curve, attack rate tables, and analytical results
Document the control measures taken and their effect
Write lessons learned and recommendations for preventing future events

description: Analyze a materials failure from visual documentation through fractography, root cause determination, and corrective action.

steps.description: Document the failed component and its surroundings before any destructive analysis.

inputs.name: failed-component
inputs.desc: The component that failed, with service history and operating conditions

inputs.name: failure-circumstances
inputs.desc: When, where, and how the failure was discovered

outputs.name: visual-documentation
outputs.desc: Photographs, measurements, and sketches of the failure in context

outputs.name: service-history-summary
outputs.desc: Operating conditions, maintenance records, and any prior issues

process: Photograph the failed component from all angles before handling
Record dimensions, orientation, and relationship to adjacent parts
Collect the service history including loads, temperatures, environment, and maintenance
Note any obvious damage patterns, corrosion products, or deformation

steps.description: Examine fracture surfaces at macro and micro scales to identify the fracture origin, propagation direction, and mode.

inputs.name: failed-component
inputs.desc: The failed part or section containing the fracture surface

outputs.name: fractographic-record
outputs.desc: Macro and SEM images of the fracture surface with annotations

outputs.name: fracture-features
outputs.desc: Identified features: beach marks, striations, chevrons, dimples, cleavage, intergranular facets

process: Examine the fracture surface under the stereomicroscope to find the origin
Identify macroscopic features (beach marks, ratchet marks, shear lips)
Examine under SEM at higher magnification for striations, dimples, or cleavage
Map the crack path relative to the microstructure

steps.description: Classify the failure mode based on the fractographic evidence and service conditions.

outputs.name: failure-mode
outputs.desc: Classified failure mode (fatigue, stress corrosion, overload, creep, hydrogen embrittlement, wear)

outputs.name: mode-evidence
outputs.desc: The specific evidence supporting the classification

process: Match the fracture features to known failure mode signatures
Cross-check with the service conditions (cyclic loading = fatigue, corrosive environment = SCC)
Consider combined or sequential modes (corrosion-fatigue, creep-fatigue)
State the failure mode with the supporting evidence chain

steps.description: Verify that the material meets its specification by testing composition, hardness, and microstructure.

inputs.name: failed-component
inputs.desc: Material samples from the failed part

inputs.name: material-specification
inputs.desc: The alloy specification and required properties

outputs.name: material-test-results
outputs.desc: Chemical composition, hardness, tensile properties, and microstructure

outputs.name: specification-compliance
outputs.desc: Pass/fail comparison of each property against the specification

process: Cut test specimens from the failed part away from the fracture
Run chemical analysis (OES, XRF, or ICP) and compare to the alloy specification
Measure hardness (Vickers, Rockwell) and compare to the required range
Prepare metallographic sections and examine the microstructure for anomalies

steps.description: Determine the root cause by combining the failure mode, material condition, and service history.

inputs.name: specification-compliance
inputs.desc: Whether the material met its specification

outputs.name: root-cause
outputs.desc: The root cause of the failure with the causal chain

outputs.name: contributing-factors
outputs.desc: Additional factors that contributed to or accelerated the failure

process: Construct the causal chain from root cause through contributing factors to failure
Distinguish between material deficiency, design deficiency, manufacturing defect, and service abuse
Evaluate whether the failure was predictable given the conditions
State the root cause with the supporting evidence from each analysis

steps.description: Compile the failure analysis into a report with visual evidence, test results, root cause, and corrective recommendations.

inputs.name: root-cause
inputs.desc: Determined root cause and causal chain

inputs.name: material-test-results
inputs.desc: Material property data and compliance status

outputs.name: failure-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Complete failure analysis report

outputs.name: corrective-actions
outputs.desc: Recommended design, material, or process changes to prevent recurrence

process: Structure the report: background, visual examination, fractography, material testing, analysis, root cause, recommendations
Include all images, test certificates, and data tables as evidence
State the root cause and contributing factors clearly
Recommend corrective actions and prioritize by effectiveness

description: Analyze particle size distribution from technique selection through measurement, distribution fitting, and batch comparison.

steps.description: Select the particle size measurement technique based on the size range, material, and required information.

inputs.name: material-description
inputs.desc: What the particles are (powder, emulsion, suspension, aerosol)

inputs.name: expected-size-range
inputs.desc: Approximate particle size range (nm, um, mm)

outputs.name: selected-technique
outputs.desc: Chosen method (laser diffraction, sieving, DLS, imaging, sedimentation) with justification

outputs.name: measurement-protocol
outputs.desc: Sample preparation and instrument settings for the selected technique

process: Map the expected size range to candidate techniques (DLS for nm, laser diffraction for um, sieving for mm)
Consider the material properties (wet vs dry, fragile, aggregating, refractive index)
Select the technique that covers the expected range with appropriate resolution
Define the sample preparation steps and instrument parameters

steps.description: Prepare the sample for measurement ensuring it is representative and properly dispersed.

inputs.name: bulk-material
inputs.desc: The bulk material from which the sample is drawn

inputs.name: measurement-protocol
inputs.desc: Preparation requirements for the selected technique

outputs.name: prepared-sample
outputs.desc: Sample ready for measurement, properly dispersed and at correct concentration

outputs.name: preparation-notes
outputs.desc: Dispersant used, sonication time, dilution factor, and any observations

process: Take a representative sub-sample using appropriate splitting (riffling, spinning, cone and quartering)
Disperse the sample in the measurement medium (wet: surfactant + sonication; dry: compressed air)
Adjust concentration to the optimal range for the instrument
Note any aggregation, settling, or dissolution observed during preparation

steps.description: Acquire the particle size measurement data with replicate runs for precision assessment.

outputs.name: raw-size-data
outputs.desc: Raw measurement output (diffraction pattern, correlation function, sieve masses, images)

outputs.name: replicate-summary
outputs.desc: Repeatability of D10, D50, D90 across replicate measurements

process: Run the background or blank measurement
Measure the sample with at least 3 replicates
Check that the obscuration (laser diffraction) or count rate (DLS) is in the valid range
Record the raw data and compute replicate statistics

steps.description: Compute the key distribution metrics (D10, D50, D90, span) from the raw size data.

outputs.name: distribution-metrics
outputs.desc: D10, D50, D90, span, and mean diameter with standard deviations

outputs.name: cumulative-distribution
outputs.desc: Cumulative and frequency distribution curves

process: Compute the volume-weighted (or number-weighted) size distribution
Calculate D10, D50, D90 from the cumulative distribution
Compute the span ((D90 - D10) / D50) as a measure of distribution width
Generate the cumulative and frequency distribution plots

steps.description: Fit a parametric distribution model to the data to describe the particle population.

inputs.name: distribution-metrics
inputs.desc: D50 and span as initial parameter estimates

outputs.name: fitted-model
outputs.desc: Best-fit distribution parameters (log-normal: mu and sigma; Rosin-Rammler: d and n)

outputs.name: goodness-of-fit
outputs.desc: R-squared, residuals, and whether the model adequately describes the data

process: Select candidate models (log-normal, Rosin-Rammler, bimodal)
Fit each model to the cumulative distribution by least squares
Compare goodness of fit and select the best model
Report the fitted parameters and their physical meaning

steps.description: Compare particle size distributions across samples or batches to detect differences.

inputs.name: distribution-metrics
inputs.desc: D10, D50, D90, and span for each sample or batch

inputs.name: specification-limits
inputs.desc: Target values and acceptance ranges if applicable

outputs.name: comparison-results
outputs.desc: Statistical comparison of distributions across samples with pass/fail against spec

outputs.name: trend-analysis
outputs.desc: Time trends in particle size if multiple batches are included

process: Overlay distribution curves from all samples for visual comparison
Test for statistically significant differences (t-test on D50, F-test on span)
Compare each sample against specification limits and flag out-of-spec results
Plot time trends if batch data spans a production period

steps.description: Compile the particle size analysis into a report with methods, distributions, model fits, and conclusions.

outputs.name: particle-size-report
outputs.desc: Complete particle size analysis report

outputs.name: data-package
outputs.desc: Raw and processed data files for archival

process: Structure the report: objective, technique, sample prep, results, comparison, conclusions
Include distribution plots, model overlays, and trend charts
State whether samples meet specification and flag any concerns
Package the raw and processed data for archival
